title: Forestry and Economic Dependencies in B.C.
summary: Explore forestry income dependency, economic diversity, vulnerability and employment concentration across 29 regional districts.
sourceNote: Source: BC Stats, Local Area Economic Profiles, 2025 release. Uses published indicator CSVs, checked against the official Excel toolkit. Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – British Columbia. Geometry is Statistics Canada 2021 census divisions already held by BCDataMapper. Model reference years 2015/2020 correspond to 2016/2021 census cycles; employment and location quotients refer to the census year. These are historical modelled estimates, not current conditions.
details: Click a district for its published forestry and income indicators. Suppressed or unreported values are never treated as zero.

Income dependency is the share of basic/external income, not the share of all household income or employment. Vulnerability is a relative index, not a probability. Descriptive colour bins are authored for this map.

This first project maps regional districts. Local-area geometry is deferred because the published Cassiar Corridor/Moricetown concordance does not reconcile. The suspect duplicated 2010/2015 cleaned census input files are not used to calculate any displayed indicator.
The 2015–2020 comparison uses one publication and current display boundaries. Pandemic effects and changes in other income sources affect the interpretation.

scenes.label: Forestry income
scenes.title: How much external income depends on forestry?
scenes.text: Compare the share of each regional economy’s basic income linked to forestry and wood manufacturing in the 2020 model. Basic income enters from outside the area and supports local activity. Select a district to read its published indicators. These are historical estimates, not current conditions.

callout.label: BC benchmark
callout.detail: Forestry share of modelled basic income, 2020. Display bins are not official risk categories.

scenes.label: Prince George region
scenes.title: Fraser-Fort George has a larger forestry dependency
scenes.text: Forestry accounts for 12.4% of modelled basic income in Fraser-Fort George, compared with 2.2% across BC. The regional district includes Prince George and surrounding communities; it is not the same geography as the Prince George local area or city.

callout.label: Fraser-Fort George
callout.detail: 2020 forestry income dependency; the separate Prince George local-area estimate is 10.5%.

scenes.label: Diversity
scenes.title: A broader income base changes the picture
scenes.text: The diversity index describes how evenly external income is spread across the model’s income sources, including government transfers and non-employment market income. Higher values mean a more even spread. It is not a count of businesses or a measure of growth.

callout.label: Regional-district range
callout.detail: 2020 published index values; the theoretical scale runs from 0 to 100.

scenes.label: Vulnerability
scenes.title: Forestry dependence and concentration combine
scenes.text: The forest vulnerability index combines forestry income dependency with economic diversity and scales the result relative to other areas. Compare regional districts within this period. A score of 100 marks the top of this comparison; it does not mean a 100% chance of a downturn.

callout.label: Bulkley-Nechako
callout.detail: Highest 2020 regional-district index. Local-area scores use a separate comparison and must not be mixed with these ranks.

scenes.label: Specialization
scenes.title: Forestry employment is concentrated in the Interior
scenes.text: The location quotient compares forestry’s share of resident employment with its share across BC. Fraser-Fort George’s 5.06 means that share is about five times the provincial share. Employment is counted by where people live, not where a mill or job is located.

callout.label: Fraser-Fort George
callout.detail: 2021 Census employment, labelled reference year 2020 in the LAEP tables.

scenes.label: 2015 baseline
scenes.title: Use the same scale to look back to 2015
scenes.text: This view uses the 2015 reference period from the same 2025 publication. The colour thresholds match the opening 2020 map. Select a district to compare both shares. The map uses the existing 2021 census-division outlines as a common display geography.

callout.label: Fraser-Fort George
callout.detail: Published forestry income dependency in the 2015 model.

scenes.label: Change
scenes.title: A falling share does not by itself measure lost jobs
scenes.text: Fraser-Fort George’s forestry dependency fell from 15.1% to 12.4%, a change of −2.7 percentage points. Shares can fall when other income sources grow. Pandemic-era transfers and employment changes affected the 2020/2021 period. Blue indicates a lower forestry share; red indicates a higher share, without assigning a good or bad outcome.

callout.label: Fraser-Fort George
callout.detail: 2020 minus 2015, using published rounded shares. This is not a forecast or a jobs-loss estimate.
